prediction.likelyOutcome: U.S. Bank is very likely to prevail on both the foreclosure and money-judgment claims given the documented default, the forbearance history, and the borrower's failure to challenge the combined pleading structure, but two years of contested bench-trial litigation signal an unidentified factual dispute that keeps this from being a near-certainty. The bigger practical question is not whether U.S. Bank wins the paper judgment near the pled $46,290,900.25, but whether the mortgaged property's value supports full collection or leaves an uncollectible deficiency, an issue the record does not address.

issues.label: In Personam Money Judgment on the Note
Propriety of Combined In Rem/In Personam Pleading
Additional Interest, Fees, and Costs Under the Loan Documents
Collectibility / Deficiency Risk on the Collateral

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court held Penn Realty breached the loan agreement and entered an in personam money judgment for U.S. Bank of $51,392,086.96 (no judgment in mortgage foreclosure was entered); the Third Circuit affirmed that judgment in a separate unpublished opinion (No. 23-2185, Sept. 25, 2024). In this precedential appeal the Third Circuit upheld the subsequent execution sale of the apartment building under Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a) and affirmed the denial of the borrower's motion to quash.
